the-naturalist-in-nicaragua: English engineer and naturalist Thomas Belt spent years working mines in Nicaragua in the 1860s and 1870s, and this book is his record of what he saw. He describes rainforest insects, birds, and plants with a scientist's care, and his notes on how species adapt to their surroundings caught the attention of Charles Darwin himself. It stands as a vivid firsthand account of Central American nature.
